title: Cross-Lingual Safety Gap Mapping: Which Languages Break Which Models

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: safety alignment is English-centric; mapping which languages bypass which models produces an immediately actionable resource for deployment teams and motivates multilingual red-teaming. Every link is explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses free translation APIs, public models via inference endpoints, and simple ASR measurement. No ML training required. Standard Python scripting with publicly available tools. Highly beginner-friendly.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: translate 50 prompts into 10 languages, run against 3-5 models, compute a language-model safety matrix. Single clear deliverable, no dependencies, obvious output artifact. Easily fits in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is substantially covered by existing work. 'Multilingual Jailbreak Challenges in Large Language Models' (ICLR 2024) created the MultiJail dataset with translations across 9+ languages and mapped safety gaps. 'A Cross-Language Investigation into Jailbreak Attacks' (arXiv:2401.16765, 2024) directly investigates cross-language jailbreaks. LinguaSafe (2025) provides a comprehensive multilingual safety benchmark. The core deliverable — a language-model safety matrix — already exists in various forms in published work. The remaining value is in updating to newer models, but the methodology and findings are established.
